thesis: Visa supports a bounded network purchase from 10% transaction/volume growth, 59.12% GAAP operating margin and substantial $15.164bn nine-month FCF. The bull decisively separates covered $3.852bn dividends from discretionary repurchases, showing operating cash remains meaningful despite excessive total distributions. Estimated 24.70x forward earnings requires durable conversion, and legal cash costs limit conviction rather than invalidating funded dividend ownership.
strongest_counterexample: FCF declined from $15.728bn and total returns of $20.282bn exceeded it; litigation and client incentives can depress incremental cash at a premium valuation, while repurchase restraint remains unannounced.
invalidation_conditions: Comparable nine-month FCF below actual cash dividends, from $15.164bn versus $3.852bn, would invalidate observed funded dividend ownership.
Comparable nine-month FCF below $15.164bn with net debt excluding restricted balances above $10.066bn and transaction growth below 10% would weaken the growth/cash compensation.
decisive_factors: Dividends leave $11.312bn FCF before buybacks; repurchase funding pressure is distinct from an uncovered payout.
Litigation cash is already real and restricted balances excluded; Visa is not evaluated as a deposit-taking bank.
